correctness.rationale: PASS: For X^m=C with C nonzero rank-one square-zero, X^(2m)=0; nilpotent Jordan theory works over every finite field. Rank J_d^m=max(d-m,0), so exactly one Jordan block has size m+1 and all other blocks are at most m. Thus every root type is (m+1) union nu with nu a partition of k=n-m-1 into parts <=m; no roots when n<=m. The centralizer is the unit group of the F_q[t]-module endomorphism algebra: semisimple quotient product M_{b_d}(F_q), radical dimension the remaining endomorphism space; consequently |Z_GL(J_lambda)|=q^(sum lambda_prime_j^2)*product_d product_i (1-q^-i). The power map commutes with conjugation and maps every permitted root orbit onto the sole rank-one nilpotent orbit, yielding each prescribed fiber A_mu/A_lambda, a positive integer. Rank n-1-len(nu) occupies exactly [m,n-1-ceil(k/m)], without gaps. The greedy bounded partition uniquely minimizes the centralizer exponent, proving maximal-rank concentration as q grows; finite enumerations independently checked q=2 n=3,4, m=2,3 (2 roots at n3 m2, 12 at n4 m2, 24 at n4 m3) by literal matrix products and ranks. All-field claims use the orbit argument, not this finite computation.
